title: Microsoft Teams: app centric management of app availability in GCC High
summary: The roadmap facts, automatic migration, licensing basis and governance controls are supported. The org-wide settings path should name the final toggle, and the blocking command needs a caveat about inconsistent examples in Microsoft's reference.

claims.where: title; front matter: products; What's changing
claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Teams app centric management.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in GCC High

claims.where: front matter: status; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.

claims.claim: Item 569433 covers GCC High.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes this feature as evolving existing app permission policies.
claims.quote: This feature evolves the existing app permission policies and provides admins with the ability to manage access to the app individually.

claims.claim: The roadmap says existing customers' policies are migrated to maintain existing app availability.
claims.quote: The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: App centric management replaces app permission policies.
claims.quote: Use the feature if already auto-migrated or manually migrate to app centric management. It replaces app permission policies.

claims.claim: Administrators manage access individually for each app in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis.

claims.claim: Everyone makes an app available to all organisation users.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: Specific users or groups restricts app availability to the selected users and groups.
claims.quote: `Specific users or groups` | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app.

claims.claim: No one makes an app unavailable to any user.
claims.quote: `No one` | Not available to any user | Same as a blocked app.

claims.claim: Administrators can set default availability for new apps published to the Teams app store.
claims.quote: First, admins can set a default value for new apps that are published to Teams app store.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Automatic migration creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.claim: Users assigned to a policy are added to its corresponding migration-created security group.
claims.quote: All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.claim: Migration assigns each policy group to the apps that its policy allowed.
claims.quote: These groups are assigned to each app they're allowed in their respective policy, maintaining their app access.

claims.claim: Automatic migration maintains existing access except for the documented policy-conflict case.
claims.quote: There's no change of app permissions during the migration, except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: In the global-allow, custom-block conflict case, migration makes the app available to all tenant users, subject to the stated EDU exception.
claims.quote: Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: For EDU customers the policy-conflict case instead makes the app available to none.
claims.quote: except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: Administrators can change the migrated availability afterwards.
claims.quote: Admins can modify this behavior as desired post migration.

claims.claim: Learn warns that not all organisations have app centric management.
claims.quote: All organizations don't have the app centric management feature available.

claims.claim: Learn points readers to MC688930 for migration timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see Message Center post MC688930 or Microsoft 365 roadmap item 151829.

claims.claim: Learn also points readers to roadmap item 151829 for timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see Message Center post MC688930 or Microsoft 365 roadmap item 151829.

claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management.

claims.quote: However, until the migration is complete, you can use the wizard and opt to complete the migration manually.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After switching, administrators cannot access, edit or use permission policies.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The completed migration cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Everyone includes guests.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: Specific users or groups excludes guests even when they are assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Assignments support security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic membership groups, nested groups and distribution lists.
claims.quote: The supported group types are security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups, and the distribution lists.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Changing membership of groups assigned to an app changes access through those groups.
claims.quote: Administrators manage these groups like any others to customize the app centric management assignments, such as adding and removing users or removing the group and replacing it with another group.

claims.claim: Previously blocked apps remain unavailable after migration.
claims.quote: After migration, your blocked apps continue to remain unavailable to users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Previously blocked apps display an unblocked status after migration.
claims.quote: The statuses of such apps show as `unblocked` now, but the apps are assigned to `No one` in the `Available to` column on the Manage apps page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Previously blocked apps receive availability No one after migration.
claims.quote: the apps are assigned to `No one` in the `Available to` column on the Manage apps page.

claims.claim: Learn describes no new autonomous behaviour for this access-management change.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" "autonomous". Read app-centric-management and manage-apps; they document access assignments, migration and governance, not new autonomous actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center cannot update app availability in bulk.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: PowerShell supports bulk availability changes using Update-M365TeamsApp.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell. For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The per-app availability control is reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets per-app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: The reference documents UsersAndGroups with -Users and -Groups for targeted availability.
claims.quote: -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Users eec823bd-0979-4cf8-9924-85bb6ffcb57d, eec823bd-0979-4cf8-9924-85bb6ffcb57e -Groups 37da2d58-fc14-453e-9a14-5065ebd63a1d

UsersandGroups

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps reaches the pane section for the org-wide third-party default.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. You can then configure the settings in the pane. Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path and the matching table cell as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps > Let users install and use available apps by default'. The setting label is given at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management#default-settings-for-app-availability, already cited by the briefing.

claims.claim: No checked Microsoft reference maps the org-wide app-default controls to a documented automation call precisely enough to give that row a call.
claims.quote: Searched: Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings GlobalApp DefaultApp PrivateApp org-wide; Teams app centric management org-wide app settings PowerShell Microsoft Graph API default availability. Read its reference, manage-apps and app-centric-management; no mapping found.

claims.claim: Microsoft apps and Custom apps settings are in the same Org-wide app settings pane.
claims.quote: You can then configure the settings in the pane. ... Under Microsoft apps ... Under Third-party apps ... Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings apply to new apps made available in the Teams app store.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings apply to:
- All the new apps made available in Teams app store.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings apply to existing apps whose availability has not been actively managed.
claims.quote: All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults do not override apps saved with Specific users and groups assignments.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: ... All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults do not override apps individually saved as Everyone or No one.
claims.quote: All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults do not override blocked apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: ... Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls the selected app's organisation-wide status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true is a documented operation for changing the app's organisation-wide state.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Keep the documented call, but append to controls[2].note and the matching table note: 'The reference describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking in Example 3, but also describes -IsBlocked $false as unblocking in Example 4; its examples do not consistently establish the Boolean polarity. Use the UI when the intended state must be unambiguous.' Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp.
